clue.text: They recorded a revolutionary kind of LP, including the ultimate in Money

indicators.note: including says the rearranged letters take the extra letter inside them
something revolutionary turns everything over, so these letters are thrown into a new order
the ultimate in a word is its final letter, here the end of the word Money

explanation.surface: A band cut a radical new sort of album with a track called Money on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges KINDOFLP into PINKFLOD; 'including' puts Y, the end of 'Money', inside it. Money is itself a famous track by the band, which makes the clue near-literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The English rock band made a string of celebrated studio albums, so they are a group who recorded.

clue.text: Bird's crest (a bit on top)

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top puts this piece above the other

parts.note: a bit is a part of something
a crest is the ridge along the top of a hill

explanation.surface: A bird's crest, with a little piece sticking up above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plump game bird of fields and hedgerows, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Can nude modelling be subtle?

indicators.note: modelling shapes material into a new form, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Asks whether posing naked for art can ever be a delicate, understated thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something with fine shades and gradations rather than broad strokes.

clue.text: Celebrated fine morning over America

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
AM, ante meridiem, marks the morning
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A lovely morning has been enjoyed across America.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone celebrated is widely known and renowned, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Workmate unaffected by turnover

definitions.note: British slang for a colleague or partner, whose letters read the same in both directions

indicators.note: unaffected by turnover says the word is unchanged when read backwards

parts.note: British slang for a colleague or partner, whose letters read the same in both directions

explanation.surface: A colleague who is not bothered by staff coming and going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like staff churn, but it means turning the word round: the answer reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for a colleague or partner, especially in the forces or police.

clue.text: He wanders off, having adjusted ready-made curtains for Queen

indicators.note: curtains for something is its end, so this letter comes last
adjusted means altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Someone drifts off after altering shop-bought curtains for the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' rearranges READYMADE into DAYDREAME; 'curtains for' looks like soft furnishings but means the end, where R goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A person lost in reverie lets the mind drift away from the present.

clue.text: To prepare for operation, U-boat takes on board 50% of ship's company

indicators.note: takes on board means takes inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a U-boat is a German submarine, a sub

indicators.note: 50% of means only half of the word is kept

parts.note: a ship's company is its crew

explanation.surface: A submarine loads half its sailors before going into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operation' suggests a military mission for the submarine, but means surgery; '50% of' keeps just the front half of the word for the sailors, and 'takes on board' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons wash hands and arms thoroughly before surgery, the standard term for that preparation.

clue.text: A Williams daughter last on Centre in the evening air

parts.note: Serena is one of the tennis-playing Williams sisters

indicators.note: last on picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A Williams sister plays the final match on Centre Court in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: Centre Court is Wimbledon's main tennis court, which suits the Williams sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: A love song sung or played outdoors at night, so it is literally a tune for the evening.

clue.text: In poor health, propping up the head of Roger Bannister

indicators.note: in a down entry, propping up puts this piece beneath the other
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ailing means unwell

explanation.surface: Roger Bannister, the first four-minute miler, holds his head up despite being unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bannister' looks like the athlete's name but is the definition: a banister is a handrail, spelt here with a misleading double N.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair handrail and its supports form a fence-like barrier along the steps.

clue.text: All aggressive (except Switzerland)

parts.note: but can mean except, as in all but one
CH, Confoederatio Helvetica, is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: Every nation is warlike apart from neutral Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes someone of tough, macho, assertive bearing, entirely forceful.

clue.text: Plan to wander around Germany with dad in retirement

indicators.note: around puts one piece outside the other

parts.note: to roam is to wander
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

indicators.note: retirement is going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pa is another word for dad

explanation.surface: A scheme to tour Germany with a retired father.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy laying out the steps ahead, the figurative sense of a route guide.

clue.text: Rumour has it you're given a snog for the white rose

indicators.note: rumour is what is heard, so the words are judged by how they are said

parts.note: a snog is a kiss, so this is you're kissed

explanation.surface: Gossip says somebody has been kissed in return for a white rose.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Wars of the Roses the House of York's emblem was the white rose; its supporters were its partisans.
explanation.definitionFit: The white rose was the badge of the House of York, standing for its supporters by metonymy.

clue.text: Compensate Robert Mugabe, discontented with military takeover

indicators.note: discontented is read as emptied of contents, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: a coup is a seizure of power by the army

explanation.surface: Robert Mugabe, the Zimbabwean leader, is paid off after being unhappy with an army takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' looks like a mood but means emptied: only the outer letters of 'Robert Mugabe' remain, R and E. Mugabe was in fact ousted by a coup in 2017.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover losses or make good on an outlay, a synonym of making up for them.

clue.text: Wave in the style of Russell?

parts.note: Russell Brand is a British comedian
the suffix -ish means somewhat like or in the manner of

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone styles themselves after comedian Russell Brand, perhaps his hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish or shake something about in the air, a synonym of waving it.

clue.text: Chit-chat about Eric?

parts.note: Eric Idle of Monty Python: tittle-tattle about him would be his surname plus a word for rumour

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means casual, pointless talk; the clue reads it as talk about the comedian Eric Idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial, unfounded chatter about other people, the everyday sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Pete's partner, eastern chap

parts.note: Pete and Dud were the comic duo Peter Cook and Dudley Moore

explanation.surface: Peter Cook's comedy partner is a man from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal American word for a man or fellow, a close synonym.

clue.text: He produced the dancers; Tosh adds reggae

indicators.note: tosh is nonsense, so these letters are made into a jumble

explanation.surface: A record producer behind a dance troupe, while Peter Tosh of the Wailers contributes reggae.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tosh' looks like the reggae star Peter Tosh but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Impressionist painted and sculpted many ballet dancers, so he produced them as artworks.

clue.text: Tossing back nips, doctor drinks whiskey in alternative to tumbler

indicators.note: tossing back means turning round, so the word is read in reverse
drinks means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rye is an American whiskey

explanation.surface: A doctor downs shots and whiskey, perhaps in place of a tumbler glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tossing back' makes SPIN of NIPS; 'tumbler' is a tumble dryer, not a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that whirls wet laundry is another way of drying clothes besides a tumble drier.

clue.text: He was in a few limp westerns

definitions.text: He was in a few limp westerns

parts.words: He was in a few limp westerns
parts.note: a cowboy hero of dozens of films, whose first name means walking unevenly

explanation.walkthrough: 'a few' is an understatement: the character starred in over sixty western films. 'limp' looks like a verdict on the films but is the hobble in his nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional cowboy got his nickname from an injury that gave him a hobbling gait.

clue.text: Freely donates fee for Steinbeck's work

indicators.note: freely means without restraint, so these letters are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone generously gives up a fee in exchange for a John Steinbeck book.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1952 novel by the American author, filmed with James Dean, is one of his best-known works.

clue.text: Stuffed with cold, revolting mucus, bishop's to die

indicators.note: stuffed with means filled with, so one piece is placed inside the other
revolting is read as turning over, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop with a streaming cold and disgusting phlegm is on his deathbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like disgust but turns MUCUS into SUCUM, which takes C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To give way, especially to illness, and so to pass away, a euphemism for dying.

clue.text: "Fruit", a reversal for 1Ac

indicators.note: a reversal turns the reference round, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: the clue number 1 is the Roman numeral I, followed by AC as written

explanation.surface: A cross-reference offering a fruit as the opposite of the band at one across.
explanation.walkthrough: '1Ac' looks like a pointer to the band at one across, but is taken literally: I (Roman one) and AC, reversed to CAI after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dark purple berry from a South American palm, marketed as a superfood.

clue.text: Diva is hard to treat with affection

parts.note: Cher is a famous pop diva
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A demanding star is difficult to be fond of.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold dear and look after lovingly, a direct synonym of the verb phrase.

clue.text: Hotel on quiet upper-class island

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
sh is a call for quiet
U is the British abbreviation for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A peaceful posh hotel on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the largest of the islands of Japan, home to Tokyo, an example of the category.

clue.text: Excerpt from verdict at Orange Free State doesn't have one!

indicators.note: Excerpt from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A legal ruling given in the Orange Free State, the old Boer republic in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orange Free State' reads as one name, but it splits: 'Orange' ends the hiding place and 'Free State' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A free state is one not ruled by an autocrat, so it lacks such a tyrant.

clue.text: He's dead keen

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
avid means keen or eager

explanation.surface: He is extremely enthusiastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead keen' reads as British slang for very eager, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name stands for any man, so a pronoun for a male person can define it.

clue.text: Party agenda's contents a bit of a fag

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its middle letters without the ends

explanation.surface: A party's agenda covers only part of a tiresome chore.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a fag is a cigarette and the slang word for its stub is the answer; a fag can also mean a chore.
explanation.definitionFit: The leftover butt of a smoked cigarette is literally a bit of one.

clue.text: A venerated character, his crown slips regularly!

indicators.note: slips regularly says letters are dropped at regular intervals, keeping every other one

explanation.surface: A revered monarch keeps letting his crown slide off.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or image treated with great reverence, a revered figure.

clue.text: Those from the Lausanne area avoid US trips

indicators.note: trips means stumbles, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Swiss people from Lausanne steer clear of American holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Lausanne is the capital of the Swiss canton of Vaud, whose people bear this French name.

clue.text: See 17
BBC boss pressing continental broadcasters to fix programming SNAFUs

indicators.note: pressing is read as holding in, so one piece is squeezed inside the other

parts.note: the head of the BBC is its Director-General, DG
the EBU is the European Broadcasting Union

explanation.surface: The BBC's chief leans on European broadcasters to sort out scheduling cock-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'programming' looks like TV schedules but means computer code.
explanation.definitionFit: Programmers remove faults from code, and SNAFUs are messes or errors.

clue.text: Clerk to imprison drug dealer

parts.note: to pen is to shut in
a pusher sells illegal drugs

explanation.surface: An official sets out to have a narcotics dealer locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A disparaging term for an office worker doing routine paperwork.
